root_cause.text: The KVM SEV code allowed synchronizing vCPU state to its VMSA after the VMSA had already been encrypted (vCPU launched), which with SNP enabled causes an RMP violation panic when the host kernel attempts to write to guest-private memory.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states "Reject synchronizing vCPU state to its associated VMSA if the vCPU has already been launched, i.e. if the VMSA has already been encrypted." The patch adds a check `if (vcpu->arch.guest_state_protected) return -EINVAL;` in `sev_es_sync_vmsa()`. The bug is confirmed by the provided Oops trace showing a crash in `sev_es_sync_vmsa` during `snp_launch_finish` on a host with SNP.
